FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2 YEARS

Colors & Shapes flashcards.

Eight colors and seven shapes, one big card each. Point at the card, then hunt for the same color on the breakfast table, in the sock drawer, at the park. The world becomes the second half of the deck.

These cards belong to Toddler 3 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name it, then hunt it

    Show the red card, then find something red in the room. The card is the starter; the real object is where the word sticks.

  2. 02

    Sort the deck

    Mix two colors together and let your toddler deal them into two piles. Messy piles are fine — sorting is the game, not the tidiness.

  3. 03

    Shape fingers

    Trace each shape with a finger, slowly, saying its name. Then trace it on the table, in the air, on your toddler's hand.

  4. 04

    Two cards at a time

    Red and blue today, circle and square tomorrow. Small sets stay fun; the whole deck at once turns into a flip-through.

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Red Flashcard for Toddlers

      Red is the loudest color in the room — fire engines, strawberries, stop signs. Most toddlers spot red first and shout it everywhere, which is exactly how color words get learned.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Makes the loudest color official — the one your toddler spots first, everywhere.

      Find one like it

      Hunt the fruit bowl together; tomatoes and apples never hide well.

      What kids learn from it

      First color words arrive loud and early; red leads the charge.

      Print tips

      Print it big; red never does subtle anyway.

      Grown-up tip

      Any shade counts — dark, bright or halfway pink; sorting comes later.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Colors and Shapes for 2-Year-Olds class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Blue Flashcard for Toddlers

      Blue is the sky card and the sea card, the color of your toddler's trousers and probably the front door. A calm, everywhere color that pairs beautifully with the yellow card for contrast.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Names the color of the sky your toddler points at from the buggy.

      Find one like it

      Check the laundry basket for anything blue — jeans always win.

      What kids learn from it

      One reliable color builds confidence to try the trickier ones next.

      Print tips

      Prop it at the window it describes.

      Grown-up tip

      A grey sky still gets reported — grey is information too.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Yellow Flashcard for Toddlers

      Yellow is sunshine, bananas and rubber ducks — the brightest card in the deck. Toddlers love the word because it feels bouncy to say: yeh-low.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Gives sunshine, bananas and egg yolks one shoutable shared name.

      Find one like it

      Hunt the kitchen for three yellow things; the banana usually surrenders first.

      What kids learn from it

      Hunting by color is visual matching, the quiet start of sorting.

      Print tips

      Print a spare for the changing bag; yellow hunts travel.

      Grown-up tip

      Golden, lemon and mustard are all yellow — saying so stretches vocabulary.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Green Flashcard for Toddlers

      Green is the outdoors color: grass, leaves, trees. This card steps straight off the page and into every walk you take, which makes green the easiest color to practise outside the house.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Turns dinner-time vegetables from suspects into a color your toddler can name.

      Find one like it

      Search the garden gate — leaves, weeds, one slightly bored snail.

      What kids learn from it

      Naming food colors makes new vegetables familiar before the first bite.

      Print tips

      Plain paper suits it; green speaks for itself.

      Grown-up tip

      Peas, beans and broccoli; eat the color together for the full lesson.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Orange Flashcard for Toddlers

      Orange is the fruit and the color in one — the rare word that is the same on both ends, which makes it twice as easy to learn. Carrots and road signs come free.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Claims the color with a fruit for a name — a toddler convenience.

      Find one like it

      Sweep the bookshelf for orange covers; picture books hoard orange.

      What kids learn from it

      A color and a fruit sharing one word doubles the practice chances.

      Print tips

      Print beside red and yellow; orange sits between them happily.

      Grown-up tip

      Marmalade at breakfast is orange evidence — point, name, carry on eating.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Purple Flashcard for Toddlers

      Purple is grapes, lavender and fancy birthday wrapping — a color that feels a bit special. It is also the trickiest color word in the set to say, which earns it extra respect.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Names the rarest color in the room, which makes every find a trophy.

      Find one like it

      Comb one room for purple, then comb the book spines again.

      What kids learn from it

      Rarity teaches attention — scarce colors get the sharpest looking.

      Print tips

      Half-size works; purple finds are rare but mighty.

      Grown-up tip

      Grapes, plums and jam jars — purple hides in kitchens most weeks.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Pink Flashcard for Toddlers

      Pink is the light one: piglets, ice cream, sugar-almond sunsets. It is also "light red" to some toddlers, which is a genuinely clever thing for them to notice — run with it.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Puts a name to the shade between red and white, found everywhere suddenly.

      Find one like it

      Hunt the bathroom — soap, sponges and the toothbrush with the lost cap.

      What kids learn from it

      Nearby shades sharpen eyes; spotting pink after red is real comparing.

      Print tips

      Keep the red card nearby for gentle comparison.

      Grown-up tip

      Pink and red look-alike days end eventually; keep both cards out.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Black Flashcard for Toddlers

      Black is the bold one — the fire truck's tyres, the cat on the fence, the night sky. High contrast makes black easy for toddler eyes to find, and "black cat" is a favourite first phrase.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Completes the set with the darkest, most dramatic color in the house.

      Find one like it

      Investigate the shoe rack; black shoes travel in pairs, hide singly.

      What kids learn from it

      Dark colors teach edges — black outlines make other colors pop.

      Print tips

      No fading worries here; black ink prints crisply every time.

      Grown-up tip

      Puddles, crows and the kettle — black turns up in good company.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Circle Flashcard for Toddlers

      The circle goes round and round — wheels, balls, plates, the moon. It is usually the first shape toddlers name, because round things fill their day from morning cup to bedtime ball.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Introduces the first shape, already known from plates, wheels and lids.

      Find one like it

      Raid the cupboards for circles — jar lids, mugs and one suspicious cookie.

      What kids learn from it

      Roundness is everywhere once named; the world gains a category today.

      Print tips

      Fridge placement recommended — the circle capital of the house.

      Grown-up tip

      Trace the circle with one finger before hunting; fingers remember shapes.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Square Flashcard for Toddlers

      Four sides, four corners, a shape that sits still — the square. Windows, crackers, cushions and cereal boxes are all squares pretending to be furniture, and your toddler gets to catch them.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Names the shape of windows, biscuits and the tiles underfoot.

      Find one like it

      Scout the living room for coasters, drawer fronts and one photo frame.

      What kids learn from it

      Four equal sides is early maths, learned standing up and pointing.

      Print tips

      Square and proud; trim the edges neatly.

      Grown-up tip

      Run a finger along each side while counting; sides and numbers bond.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Triangle Flashcard for Toddlers

      Three sides and a pointy top — the triangle, the roof of every house your toddler will ever draw. Pizza slices and mountains give it a real life outside the card.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Introduces three sides — the shape of roofs, mountains and stubborn sandwich quarters.

      Find one like it

      Scan the rooftops from the window; every roofline hides a triangle.

      What kids learn from it

      Counting sides works here — three is easier to hold than four.

      Print tips

      Hang it beside square; the side-count difference does the teaching.

      Grown-up tip

      Napkins fold into triangles twice — fold, hunt, unfold, repeat.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Rectangle Flashcard for Toddlers

      A square stretched long — four sides, two short and two long. Doors, tables, books and screens are all rectangles, which quietly makes this the most-seen shape of the whole day.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Explains the stretched square behind doors, books and butter boxes.

      Find one like it

      Try doors and drawers — rectangles hold the house shut, mostly.

      What kids learn from it

      Same shape, different lengths — comparison starts quietly here.

      Print tips

      Portrait orientation for once; rectangles appreciate the taller frame.

      Grown-up tip

      A door is the biggest rectangle at home; measure yourselves against it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Star Flashcard for Toddlers

      The star shape with points to count, straight off the night sky and the top of the Christmas tree. It is the shape toddlers want to draw first, usually with great enthusiasm and five extra points.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Catches the shape toddlers see twice — on cards and, later, actually outside.

      Find one like it

      Watch the night sky from a warm windowsill; one star is a win.

      What kids learn from it

      Pointing at tiny far things builds focus, patience and wonder.

      Print tips

      Go small on this one; stars are modest about such things.

      Grown-up tip

      On cloudy nights the card stands in, no apologies needed.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Heart Flashcard for Toddlers

      The heart shape — the one that means love, valentines and every drawing your toddler will ever make for you. It has one point at the bottom and two bumps at the top, and it is pure fun to trace.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Hands over the shape your toddler already draws — two bumps and a point.

      Find one like it

      Raid the greeting-card drawer; hearts shelter in small paper everywhere.

      What kids learn from it

      Pairs a first feeling word with something drawable — meaning sticks.

      Print tips

      Extra copies suggested; heart cards get given away as gifts.

      Grown-up tip

      Accept lopsided hearts instantly; lopsided ones carry more, somehow.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · COLORS & SHAPES · AGES 2 YEARS

      Oval Flashcard for Toddlers

      The oval is the egg shape — a circle gently stretched. It rolls wobbly instead of smooth, which makes it the surprise shape of the deck: round, but not a circle.

      Teaching tips

      What this card shows

      Completes the shapes with the gentle one — a circle that stretched in its sleep.

      Find one like it

      Sweep the kitchen for ovals — spoon bowls, a lemon, the fish slice.

      What kids learn from it

      Almost-round is its own idea, and ovals prove it patiently.

      Print tips

      Run it after circle; ovals read best as a sequel.

      Grown-up tip

      Lay the circle card beside it; the difference argues for itself.

      Teach it, step by step
